results.title: Barnea's question on just finite presentations (Kourovka 21.10)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every finite group $G$ has a just finite presentation: a presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $X$ and $R$ finite that defines $G$ and such that removing any single relator from $R$ gives a presentation of an infinite group.

results.title: Every finite group has a just finite presentation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite group $G$ there are a natural number $n$ and a finite subset $R$ of the free group on $n$ generators $x_1, \dots, x_n$ such that the group $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ is isomorphic to $G$ and, for every $r \in R$, the group $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \setminus \{r\} \rangle$ is infinite. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 21.10 is positive.

results.title: Commutator for Engel lengths
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For elements $x$ and $y$ of a group, the commutator is $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$ (the convention of the Kourovka Notebook).

results.title: Iterated commutators for Engel lengths
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For elements $h$ and $g$ of a group and a natural number $l$, the iterated commutator $[h, g; l]$ is defined by $[h, g; 0] = h$ and $[h, g; l + 1] = [[h, g; l], g]$, where $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$; in particular $[h, g; 1] = [h, g]$.

results.title: Bounded Engel element
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An element $g$ of a group $G$ is an Engel element if there is an $l \ge 1$ such that $[h, g; l] = 1$ for every $h \in G$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$, $[h, g; i + 1] = [[h, g; i], g]$ and $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$.

results.title: Engel length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an element $g$ of a group $G$, the Engel length $l(g)$ is the least $k \ge 1$ such that $[h, g; k] = 1$ for every $h \in G$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$, $[h, g; i + 1] = [[h, g; i], g]$ and $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$. If no such $k$ exists, that is, if $g$ is not an Engel element, then $l(g) = 0$.

results.title: Engel lengths of products admit no polynomial bound (Kourovka 11.88)

results.summary: There is a group $G$ such that for every polynomial $\varphi(x, y)$ in two variables with natural-number coefficients there are $u, v \in G$ such that $u$, $v$ and $uv$ are Engel elements and $l(uv) > \varphi(l(u), l(v))$. Here $g \in G$ is an Engel element if there is a $k \ge 1$ with $[h, g; k] = 1$ for all $h \in G$, and its Engel length $l(g)$ is the least such $k$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$,…

results.title: Engel element
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An element $g$ of a group $G$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ there is an $n \ge 0$ with $h_n = 1$, where $h_0 = h$ and $h_{i + 1} = [h_i, g]$ with $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$; that is, some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial.

results.title: Bludov's problem on Engel elements in simple groups (Kourovka 16.17)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that no non-abelian simple group contains an Engel element other than the identity: for every simple group $G$ with elements $a$, $b$ such that $ab \ne ba$, every Engel element $g$ of $G$ satisfies $g = 1$. Here $g$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial, where $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$.

results.title: Non-abelian simple groups can have nontrivial Engel elements (Kourovka 16.17)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a non-abelian simple group $G$ (one with elements $a$, $b$ such that $ab \ne ba$) that contains an Engel element $g \ne 1$. Here $g$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial, where $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$.

results.title: Right Engel element
results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the ambient space is the real Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$, with coordinates indexed by $0, \dots, n-1$ and the Euclidean norm.

results.title: Unit sphere in Euclidean space
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the unit sphere $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ at Euclidean distance $1$ from the origin.

results.title: Model hyperplane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \ge 1$, the model hyperplane in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of points $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ whose first coordinate $x_0$ is $0$. It is the local model for a locally flat embedded sphere.

results.title: Locally flat maps of the sphere
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be the unit sphere and let $H = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : x_0 = 0\}$ be the model hyperplane. A map $c : S^{n-1} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is locally flat if for every point $p \in S^{n-1}$ there are open sets $U, V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with $c(p) \in U$ and a homeomorphism $h : U \to V$ such that $h(U \cap c(S^{n-1})) = V \cap H$.

results.title: Locally flat embedded sphere
results.caption: Structure

results.title: Inside of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the inside of $S$ is the set of points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in the complement $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus S$ is bounded.

results.title: Region between two flat spheres

The region between $f$ and $g$ is the closure of the inside of the image of $f$ with the inside of the image of $g$ removed, where the inside of a set $S$ is the set of points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus S$ is bounded.

results.title: Stochastic matrix
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a natural number $M$, a stochastic matrix of size $M + 1$ is a square matrix $P = (P_{ij})$ indexed by the states $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$, with real entries $P_{ij} \ge 0$ for all states $i, j$, whose rows sum to $1$: $\sum_j P_{ij} = 1$ for every $i$. It is the transition matrix of a Markov chain on these $M + 1$ states.

results.title: Matrix powers of a stochastic matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th matrix power $P^n$ is defined by $P^0 = I$, the identity matrix, and $(P^{n+1})_{ij} = \sum_k P(i, k) (P^n)_{kj}$. The entry $(P^n)_{ij}$ is the probability of moving from state $i$ to state $j$ in exactly $n$ steps.

results.title: Irreducible stochastic matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ and write $P^n$ for its $n$-th matrix power. Then $P$ is irreducible if for all states $i$ and $j$ there is an $n \ge 1$ with $(P^n)_{ij} > 0$; that is, every state can be reached from every state, itself included, in a positive number of steps.

results.title: Probability distribution on a finite state space
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A probability distribution on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ is a function $\pi$ from the states to $\mathbb{R}$ with $\pi(i) \ge 0$ for every state $i$ and $\sum_i \pi(i) = 1$.

results.title: Stationary distribution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A probability distribution $\pi$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ is stationary for a stochastic matrix $P$ on the same states if $\pi P = \pi$, that is, $\sum_i \pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j)$ for every state $j$.

results.title: Detailed balance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A probability distribution $\pi$ and a stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ satisfy the detailed balance (reversibility) equations when $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i$ and $j$.

results.title: Reversible stochastic matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ is reversible if there is a probability distribution $\pi$ on the states that is stationary for $P$ and satisfies the detailed balance equations $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i, j$.

results.title: Kolmogorov's cycle condition
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ satisfies Kolmogorov's cycle condition when (1) for all states $x, y$, $P(x, y) > 0$ implies $P(y, x) > 0$; and (2) for every $n \ge 0$ and every loop of states $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$ with $x_n = x_0$ and $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} P(x_{i+1}, x_i) > 0$, we have $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} P(x_i, x_{i+1}) = \prod_{i=0}^{n-1} P(x_{i+1}, x_i)$.

results.title: Detailed balance implies stationarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ and let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the same states. If $\pi$ and $P$ satisfy the detailed balance equations $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i, j$, then $\pi$ is stationary for $P$: $\sum_i \pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j)$ for every state $j$.

results.title: Powers of a stochastic matrix are nonnegative
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Every entry of every power of a stochastic matrix is nonnegative.

results.title: Detailed balance distributions of irreducible chains are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$. If a probability distribution $\pi$ satisfies the detailed balance equations $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i, j$, then $\pi(i) > 0$ for every state $i$.

results.title: Forward path product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$ and a path of states $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k$, the path product is the real number $\prod_{i=0}^{k-1} P(x_i, x_{i+1})$, the product of the forward transition probabilities along the path. For the empty path and for a path consisting of a single state it is $1$.

results.title: Path products are nonnegative
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$. For every path (finite list of states), the product of the forward transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along the path is nonnegative.

results.title: Ratio product along a path
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$ and a path of states $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k$, the ratio product is the real number $\prod_{i=0}^{k-1} \frac{P(x_i, x_{i+1})}{P(x_{i+1}, x_i)}$, where a quotient with denominator $0$ is taken to be $0$. For the empty path and for a path consisting of a single state it is $1$.

results.title: The ratio product is nonnegative
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$, the ratio product along every path of states is nonnegative.

results.title: Positive paths have positive ratio product
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix such that $P(x, y) > 0$ implies $P(y, x) > 0$ for all states $x$ and $y$. If the forward path product along a path of states is positive, then the ratio product along that path is positive.

results.title: Paths from positive matrix powers
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$. If $n > 0$ and the $(i, j)$ entry of the $n$-th matrix power $P^n$ is positive, then there is a path from $i$ to $j$ (a finite list of states starting at $i$ and ending at $j$) along which the product of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ is positive.

results.title: Irreducible chains have positive paths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$. For any two states $i, j$ there is a path from $i$ to $j$ (a finite list of states starting at $i$ and ending at $j$) along which the product of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ is strictly positive.

results.title: First step of the ratio product
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix, $n$ a natural number and $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n+1}$ states. Then the ratio product along $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n+1}$ equals $\frac{P(c_0, c_1)}{P(c_1, c_0)}$ times the ratio product along $c_1, \dots, c_{n+1}$, where a quotient with denominator $0$ is taken to be $0$.

results.title: The ratio product as a finite product
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix, $n$ a natural number and $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_n$ states. Then the ratio product along $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_n$ equals $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \frac{P(c_i, c_{i+1})}{P(c_{i+1}, c_i)}$, where a quotient with denominator $0$ is taken to be $0$.

results.title: The ratio product around a loop is one
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix satisfying Kolmogorov's cycle condition, and let $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$ be a path of states with $n \ge 1$ and $x_0 = x_n$ such that $P(x_{i+1}, x_i) > 0$ for every $i < n$. Then the ratio product along $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$ equals $1$.

results.title: Cycle weight
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$ and fix a reference state $i_0$. The cycle weight of a state $j$ relative to $i_0$ is the product of the ratios $P(x, y) / P(y, x)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along a path (a finite list of states) from $i_0$ to $j$ whose product of transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states is positive, where a ratio with $P(y, x) = 0$…

results.title: Ratio product of joined paths
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix and let $x_0, \dots, x_k$ and $y_0, \dots, y_l$ be paths of states with $x_k = y_0$. Then the ratio product along the joined path $x_0, \dots, x_k, y_1, \dots, y_l$ equals the ratio product along $x_0, \dots, x_k$ times the ratio product along $y_0, \dots, y_l$.

results.title: Positive path products have positive steps
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$, and let $l$ be a path (a finite list of states) whose $i$-th state, counting from $0$, is $l_i$. If the product of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along $l$ is positive, then $P(l_i, l_{i+1}) > 0$ for every $i$ such that $i + 1$ is less than the length of $l$.

results.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$, and let $l_1, l_2$ be nonempty paths (finite lists of states) such that the last state of $l_1$ is the first state of $l_2$. results.title: Path independence of cycle weight

results.title: Eventually periodic sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ with values in a type $\alpha$ is eventually periodic if there are natural numbers $p > 0$ (a period) and $n_0$ (a preperiod) such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$.

results.title: Explicit period and preperiod give eventual periodicity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type and $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ a sequence. If there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0$ such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$, then $u$ is eventually periodic.

results.title: Period and preperiod of an eventually periodic sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type. If a sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is eventually periodic, then there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0$ such that $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every natural number $n \ge n_0$.

results.title: Periodic sequences are eventually periodic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be a sequence and let $p > 0$ be a natural number with $u(n + p) = u(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $u$ is eventually periodic.

results.title: Ultimately periodic sequences
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type. A sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is called ultimately periodic exactly when it is eventually periodic; the two terms name the same notion.

results.title: Orbits in a finite set are eventually periodic

results.title: Graphs with a $K_5$ minor

results.summary: A simple graph $G$ has $K_5$ as a minor if there are five nonempty, pairwise disjoint sets of vertices $S_1, \dots, S_5$ such that any two vertices in the same set are joined by a walk in $G$ all of whose vertices lie in that set, and for all distinct $i, j$ some vertex of $S_i$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex of $S_j$.

results.title: Graphs with a $K_{3,3}$ minor

results.title: Planarity by forbidden minors

results.title: Four color theorem

results.title: External neighbourhood
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a vertex set $V$ and a set $A \subseteq V$, the external neighbourhood of $A$ in $G$ is the set of vertices $v \notin A$ that are adjacent in $G$ to some vertex of $A$.

results.title: Membership in the external neighbourhood
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$, let $A \subseteq V$ and let $v \in V$. Then $v$ lies in the external neighbourhood of $A$ in $G$ if and only if $v \notin A$ and $v$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex $a \in A$.

results.title: The external neighbourhood is disjoint from the set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every simple graph $G$ on a vertex set $V$ and every set $A \subseteq V$, the external neighbourhood of $A$ in $G$ is disjoint from $A$.

results.title: External neighbours have a neighbour in the set
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: C-expander
results.caption: Definition

Then $G$ is a $C$-expander if $C > 0$, every set $A \subseteq V$ with $|A| < n/(2C)$ has an external neighbourhood in $G$ with at least $C|A|$ vertices, and for any two disjoint sets $A, B \subseteq V$ with $|A| \ge n/(2C)$ and $|B| \ge n/(2C)$ some vertex of $A$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex of $B$.

results.title: The parameter of a C-expander is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $C$ be a real number. If $G$ is a $C$-expander, then $C > 0$.

results.title: Small sets expand in a $C$-expander
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a real number and let $G$ be a $C$-expander on a finite vertex set $V$. Then every set $A \subseteq V$ with $|A| < |V|/(2C)$ has at least $C|A|$ external neighbours, that is, at least $C|A|$ vertices outside $A$ are adjacent to some vertex of $A$.

results.title: Large disjoint sets in a C-expander span an edge

results.title: Uniform vertex expander

results.title: The parameter of a uniform vertex expander is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $h$ be a real number. If $G$ is a uniform vertex expander with parameter $h$, then $h > 0$.

results.title: Small sets expand in a uniform vertex expander

results.title: List-coloring instances

results.title: Well-formed list-coloring instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list-coloring instance $(n, E, L)$ is well formed when the edge list $E$ has no repeated entries, every edge $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$ and its reversal $(v, u)$ does not occur in $E$, and the list $L$ of color lists has length $n$.

results.title: Feasible list-coloring instances

results.title: The final layer of the odd-even merger has depth at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $k$, the final layer of the odd-even merger on $2^{k+2}$ wires, which compares wires $2i + 1$ and $2i + 2$ for each $i < 2^{k+1} - 1$, has depth at most $1$: its comparators are disjoint.

results.title: Depth bound for Batcher's odd-even merger
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $k$, Batcher's odd-even merger on $2^{k+1}$ wires has depth at most $k + 1$.

results.title: Depth bound for Batcher's odd-even merge sort as a comparator list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $k$, there is a $d$ with $2d \le k(k+1)$ such that the comparator list of Batcher's odd-even merge sort on wires $0, \dots, 2^k - 1$ has depth at most $d$; that is, its depth is at most $k(k+1)/2$.

results.title: Depth bound for Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $k$, there is a $d$ with $2d \le k(k+1)$ such that Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network on $2^k$ wires has depth at most $d$; that is, its depth is at most $k(k+1)/2$.

results.title: Lower bound for the depth of Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all $k$ and $d$, if Batcher's odd-even merge sorting network on $2^k$ wires has depth at most $d$, then $k \le d$.

results.title: Surviving weight of a GPS event
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The surviving weight `max (N j - α) 0` of event `j`, for expected read counts `N` and sparseness parameter `α`.

results.title: The GPS M-step with component elimination
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `π j = max (N j - α) 0 / ∑ k, max (N k - α) 0`.

results.title: Expected penalized complete-data log-likelihood of GPS
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected complete-data log penalized likelihood of GPS, up to an additive constant: `∑ j, (N j - α) log (π j)` (the expected log-likelihood `∑ j, N j log (π j)` plus the log of the negative Dirichlet prior). Meaningful for positive `π`.

results.title: Truncated GPS objective
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The truncated objective `∑ j, max (N j - α) 0 * log (π j)`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of surviving weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Surviving weights are nonnegative.

results.title: Total surviving weight is positive iff some event survives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The total surviving weight is positive iff some event has `α < N j`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the GPS M-step update
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The update is nonnegative.

results.title: GPS M-step update sums to one when some event survives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The update sums to one when some event survives.

results.title: Elimination
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: When some event survives, event `j` gets probability zero iff `N j ≤ α`.

results.title: GPS M-step keeps positive probability exactly on surviving events
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: When some event survives, event `j` keeps positive probability iff `α < N j`.

results.title: GPS M-step at zero sparseness is the ordinary mixture M-step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With `α = 0` and nonnegative counts the update is the ordinary mixture M-step `N j / ∑ N`.

results.title: The update is an upper bound for the truncated objective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The update is an upper bound for the truncated objective over the positive probability vectors (derived characterization of the elimination rule). Upper-bound statement only: this does not prove the value at `mStep` is the supremum (no approximation or `sSup` theorem is given). When elimination occurs `mStep` itself is not a positive vector (eliminated coordinates are zero), so it is the boundary point on the face…

results.title: Truncated and penalized objectives agree when every event survives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: When every event survives, the penalized and truncated objectives agree.

results.title: GPS M-step formula when every event survives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: When every event survives, the update is `(N j - α) / ∑ k, (N k - α)`.

results.title: The M-step of the restructured model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: When every remaining event survives (`α < N j` for all `j`), the update maximizes the GPS expected complete-data log penalized likelihood over the positive probability vectors.
